title: Dhamaal 4 Crosses ₹170 Crore Worldwide as Ajay Devgn Comedy Enters Bollywood's 100-Crore Club
excerpt: The franchise's fourth instalment surpassed Total Dhamaal's opening-week record and has become Bollywood's fifth highest-grossing film of 2026, though The Odyssey now threatens its screen count.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dhamaal 4 has grossed over ₹170 crore worldwide in just 10 days.
  • The film is now Bollywood's fifth highest-grossing film of 2026.
  • It set a franchise record with a ₹96 crore opening week.
  • Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey has reduced Dhamaal 4's screen count to 45% of its original.
  • The film's North American collections reached approximately ₹6.5 crore.

  • Dhamaal 4 has crossed ₹170 crore in worldwide gross collection after 10 days, with an India net of approximately ₹124 crore
  • The film became Bollywood's fifth entry into the 100-crore club in 2026, surpassing Cocktail 2's lifetime collection
  • It set a franchise record with a ₹96 crore opening week, beating Total Dhamaal's previous high of ₹94.55 crore
  • Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey has taken over premium screens, leaving Dhamaal 4 with roughly 45 percent of its original screen count

Dhamaal 4, the latest instalment in one of Bollywood's most bankable comedy franchises, has crossed ₹170 crore in worldwide gross collection after 10 days in theatres — comfortably entering the 100-crore club and staking its claim as one of the year's biggest Hindi hits.

The Ajay Devgn-led comedy recorded an India net collection of approximately ₹124 crore and an overseas gross of nearly ₹20 crore through its second weekend, according to tracking data from Sacnilk and Koimoi. It has become Bollywood's fifth highest-grossing film of 2026 globally, overtaking Cocktail 2 (₹166 crore) and trailing only the year's mega-grossers: Dhurandhar 2 (₹1,850 crore), Border 2 (₹485 crore), Bhooth Bangla (₹292 crore), and Welcome to the Jungle (₹193 crore).

A Franchise Record

Directed by Indra Kumar, the film closed its first week with ₹96 crore net in India, surpassing Total Dhamaal's previous franchise high of ₹94.55 crore. The opening weekend was particularly strong: ₹14 crore on Thursday, ₹22.5 crore on Friday, and ₹28.5 crore on Sunday. Weekday collections dipped as expected — ranging from ₹6 crore to ₹9.5 crore — before the second weekend delivered a strong bounce.

Saturday's occupancy data tells the story of a film that has found its audience through word of mouth. Dhamaal 4 recorded 39.35 percent overall Hindi occupancy across 8,712 shows, with evening screenings hitting 56.46 percent — the kind of numbers that signal strong family repeat viewing.

The Odyssey Factor

The film faces a significant headwind starting this week. Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, which opened to a record-breaking $264 million worldwide debut, has claimed the lion's share of premium screens — including all IMAX and large-format allocations. Dhamaal 4 is now operating on roughly 45 percent of its original screen count.

The squeeze means the franchise's path to ₹200 crore worldwide — a target that looked achievable after the first weekend — now depends entirely on how well the film holds in general screenings through the week. Analysts expect the film to benefit from the lack of major Bollywood competition until late July, but the premium-screen losses will cap its daily ceiling.

Ensemble Chemistry Carries the Day

Produced on a reported budget of around ₹200 crore, Dhamaal 4 brings back the franchise's core trio of Devgn, Arshad Warsi, and Riteish Deshmukh alongside Jaaved Jaaferi, with Ravi Kishan, Sanjay Mishra, Sanjeeda Shaikh, and Esha Gupta joining the ensemble. Reviews have been mixed — the film holds no pretensions beyond slapstick — but audiences have clearly decided that the formula still works.

In the NRI belt, the film has performed respectably, with North American collections reaching $777,000 (approximately ₹6.5 crore) through the first week. The comedy genre has historically travelled well in the diaspora, where Bollywood comedies often serve as communal viewing events for Indian families abroad.
